item.title:
On the night of May 5th, the preschool attached to Park East Synagogue on Manhattan’s Upper East Side closed early because staff could not guarantee a safe dismissal of the children in their care. Outside, more than 200 antizionist protesters had surrounded the building while waving Hezbollah flags, tearing down an image of the Lubavitcher Rebbe, and screaming “Death to the IDF,” “Rapists,” and “Zionist trash” at Jewish New Yorkers trying to get through the synagogue’s doors.
The pro-terrorist agitators mobbed NYPD officers and tried to push past protective barricades; rioting that injured one officer who had to be taken to the hospital.
The ADL documented chants from the Jew-hating mob calling for “intifada” and celebrating terrorist “martyrs.” Shamefully, no one was arrested — undoubtedly pleasing the city’s anti-Israel bigot of a mayor, Zohran Mamdani.
After the Jewish children at Park East were unable to attend school for a full day as usual — after the mob of racists had laid siege to the house of worship — Mamdani’s office issued a statement justifying the mob’s behavior, saying that “sacred spaces should not be used to promote activities in violation of international law.”
That statement itself was racist and deeply offensive to Jews, who don’t take their cues about what they can or cannot do on their own properties from a hateful mayor who despises them.
The mayor’s response, it will likely turn out, was also illegal.
